question: UCLA Foundation DAF line audit: read its FY2021-25 Schedule D Part I and audited financial statements and resolve the sign of DAF grants (filed -$109.7m FY2023 and -$120.3m FY2024; DAFRC shows +$109.7m for FY2023 and keeps an imputed +$169.9m for FY2024) and the 10-11 accounts holding about $0.6bn
conclusion_affected: Institutional segment contributions and grants FY2022-24; UCLA is about 17% of segment assets
rationale: One sponsor with 10-11 DAFs drives the segment's contribution swings ($0.28bn -> $0.85bn -> $0.56bn -> $0.25bn). Its filed grants are negative and the corrections file keeps an imputed value, so segment flows are unreliable until this is settled

question: Universite de Montreal (EIN 237172320) DAF classification: confirm whether its $390-429m 'DAF' value (657-714 accounts, $0 contributions and $0 grants FY2021-23; filed $0 for FY2024 while DAFRC keeps an imputed $427.1m) is a real DAF programme or endowment-style funds mis-entered in the DAF column; propose an R-rule if not
conclusion_affected: Institutional segment assets (12% of FY2024 segment assets) and the segment share trend
rationale: $0 flows on $0.4bn for three years is not DAF behaviour, and the FY2024 filed return reports $0. Removing it would cut the institutional segment's FY2024 assets from $3.59bn to $3.16bn

question: Host-retention point estimates from the sponsor side: for the 12 programmes with a published host minimum (Stanford, Columbia, Yale, UCLA, Rochester, Cornell, MSU, UND, Brown, Penn, Harvard, Mayo), read audited financial statements or annual DAF reports for internal distributions to the host, which never appear on Schedule I when the sponsor is the institution
conclusion_affected: Whether institutional DAFs are 'restricted-purpose' in practice (current bound for FY2024 sample: 6%-69% of DAF grants stay with the host)
rationale: Schedule I bounds are wide because self-sponsoring universities pay DAF grants to themselves internally; only labelled filers (Harvard, Yale, MIT, Dartmouth) and DAF-only foundations (Cornell University Foundation) give tight figures

question: Off-panel institutional DAF programmes: test universities and health systems that publish in-house DAF terms but have no DAFRC row (e.g. University of Pennsylvania, Michigan State, University of North Dakota Foundation, Johns Hopkins) against their Schedule D Part I and Schedule D Part V/Part XIII to see whether DAF balances are reported in the 'other funds' column or inside endowment
conclusion_affected: Count and size of the institutional segment (currently 165-174 DAFRC sponsors with positive assets)
rationale: Several programmes with published terms do not appear in the DAFRC panel or in the repo's non-DAFRC Schedule D filer list as education/health names, so the panel count is a floor

question: SUNY Binghamton Foundation FY2024 DAF-to-DAF transfer: confirm what the $84.18m 'unrestricted support' grant to Greater Horizons (EIN 200849590) was (a fund migration from the university DAF programme to a community-foundation sponsor?) and whether R5 netting in dafrc-market-totals-netted.csv already removes it
conclusion_affected: R5 netting of DAF-to-DAF flows; institutional segment grants FY2024
